# `¿` — Roll / Deal

Function. Keys: `Alt-/`. Hanzi: `掷/抽` (`擲/抽`). Ranks: `0` monadic, `0 0` dyadic

`¿N`: uniform draw from `⍳N`. `¿0`: U(0,1). Pervasive.

```bpl
¿6 ∊ ⍳6ₓ           ⍝ $t
```

`M¿N`: `M` draws without replacement from `⍳N`.

```bpl
≢3¿10             ⍝ 3ₓ
≢∪3¿10            ⍝ 3ₓ
```

Bounds are nonnegative whole numbers; `M≤N`. Exact arguments give exact integer draws. Where integers wrap, under static kinds or at a fixed width, a roll of integers gives integers, and a bound of 0, which rolls a float, is a DOMAIN error. A float bound of 0 still rolls a float, as `¿0` does. Dyalog APL writes Roll and Deal as `?`, which BPL uses for [predicates](question.qmd).

`¿` draws from the session's generator, which the operating system keys when the session starts. [`•prefs ["seed":n]`](../system/prefs.qmd) seeds it with the nonnegative whole number `n`. [`•rand`](../system/rand.qmd) makes a separate generator and describes how draws advance its stream, including in maps.

```bpl
•prefs ["seed":42] ⋄ a←¿6 6 6 ⋄ •prefs ["seed":42] ⋄ a≡¿6 6 6    ⍝ $t
```
